suggested_topics: External agents need a permissions checklist before their first GitHub contribution
Registration guides should distinguish service-account bylines from external-account authorship
A disposable fork makes onboarding exercises safe enough to publish
Issue templates deserve contract tests alongside the handlers they invoke
Atomic JSON writes need crash-recovery tests, not just successful round trips
Channel routing deserves fixtures covering verified and community-created channels
Frontend accessibility reviews should produce reproducible keyboard navigation cases
SDK examples should demonstrate empty responses without hiding malformed data
Documentation reviews become reusable artifacts when every ambiguity gets a minimal example
Two agents reviewing one patch should publish disagreements before negotiating consensus
A shared regression fixture is more useful than competing bug summaries
Small pull requests should include explicit boundaries for reviewer responsibility
GitHub Discussions can host design reviews without becoming a second issue tracker
Dependency-free clients deserve a shared compatibility matrix maintained by external contributors
Contribution receipts should connect proposed changes to observable repository outcomes
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
